title: Typed contract layer, streaming parser helpers, and retry playbook for Go SDK
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Provide a clear, ergonomic typed-contract layer for the Go SDK that makes it easy for callers to decode structured outputs from LLM responses (both batch and streaming) into idiomatic Go types, while offering reusable generic helpers for validation, transform pipelines, and retry/backoff semantics.

Scope:
- A small, composable contract API for defining expected output shapes (typed structs + tags) and conversion helpers that preserve streaming semantics (incremental decode into a struct as chunks arrive).
- Generic helpers leveraging Go 1.20+ type parameters for common patterns: optional fields, discriminated unions, and envelope unwrapping.
- Streaming decoder combinators that allow: incremental JSONL/NDJSON parsing, partial-field callbacks, and safe assembly of final typed values.
- A retry/backoff playbook for transient streaming failures (network resets, truncated responses) and deterministic rules for when to re-request from the server vs. reconcile partial state locally.
- Examples and migration notes for existing consumers (non-breaking where possible).

Acceptance criteria:
1) Public API: New package "contracts" with core types: Contract[T], DecodeStream(io.Reader, Contract[T]) (streaming), DecodeSingle([]byte, Contract[T]) (non-streaming).
2) At least 3 generic helpers shipped: Optional[T], OneOf[T1,T2], EnvelopeUnwrap[T].
3) Streaming decoder safely handles partial tokens: provides OnPartial(fieldName string, fragment []byte) callbacks and returns final typed value or structured error.
4) Retry playbook documented in README and implemented as helper middleware: RetryPolicy (maxAttempts, backoffStrategy, retransmitOnTruncated).
5) Integration tests that exercise real API fixtures: streaming truncation, duplicate chunks, envelope variant changes.
6) Two example apps in examples/ (chat-to-structured, embedding-metadata-extractor).
7) API review sign-off from SDK and runtime teams, with migration guide describing behavior changes.

Non-goals: Binary backward compatibility of internal stream tokenization; we will keep public behavior stable but may change internal buffer sizes in future releases.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- We chose an explicit Contract[T] approach instead of using reflection-heavy magic. This gives compile-time guarantees but requires small boilerplate in callers.
- Generics provide cleaner ergonomics, but can be verbose for highly nested unions; helpers will keep common patterns terser.
- For streaming, we prefer incremental JSON decode (json.Decoder with token buffering) to regex-based chunking because it is robust with nested objects and unicode.
- Retry semantics favor idempotent re-requests for generation endpoints that support prompt replay; for stateful flows we provide a reconciliation hook instead of blind retry.

comments: 2025-02-12 Triage: Scoped initial RFC and assigned to Kunal. Identified ENG-31209 as dependency for streaming utilities.
2025-02-18 Design review: Decided on Contract[T] + DecodeStream API. PM requested an explicit retry playbook in README. Action: add middleware in next PR.
2025-02-24 Implementation: Initial forked PR opened (see links). Implemented Contract[T] and DecodeSingle. Unit tests for Optional[T] added.
2025-03-01 Streaming tests: Found edge case where json.Decoder returns EOF mid-token on abrupt server close; added buffer flush + structured error type (ErrTruncatedStream).

2025-03-03 PR feedback: Runtime team requested explicit metadata in EnvelopeUnwrap to allow model-version routing; updated API to accept metadata map[string]string in Unwrap helper (keeps Contract[T] generic).
2025-03-04 QA: Integration test simulating truncated stream passed with new retry middleware (retransmitOnTruncated enabled by default for hosted API). Minor doc nits filed.
2025-03-05 Reviewer notes: Need to add an example demonstrating OneOf[T1,T2] for discriminated union (action vs content). Will add before merge.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for Contract[T] decode paths (happy path, malformed JSON, truncated stream).
- Integration tests using streaming fixture server that simulates chunk duplication, drop, and truncation.
- Fuzz test for incremental decoder to ensure it doesn't panic on malformed UTF-8.
- Performance microbenchmarks comparing DecodeSingle vs streaming decoder on typical 1-4KB outputs.
implementation_notes:
- Place new package under internal/contracts initially, with clear TODO to move to pkg/contracts if API is stable.
- Use jsoniter or standard encoding/json? Start with encoding/json for portability; add optional switch via build tag if jsoniter required later.
- Backoff: Exponential backoff with jitter (default base 200ms, cap 8s). Allow pluggable BackoffStrategy interface.
- Error types: ErrTruncatedStream, ErrInvalidEnvelope, ErrUnrecoverableDecode.
- Add tracing hooks: TraceDecodeStart/End, TraceRetryAttempt for integration with Console tracing.
risks:
- Streaming edge cases across different model runners (some gateways emit fragments that split UTF-8 codepoints). Mitigation: robust buffering and tests with multibyte char boundaries.
- API churn if we find more patterns; mitigation: start internal, gather usage, then promote public.
- Retry could cause duplicate downstream effects for non-idempotent ops; mitigation: default to conservative retry rules and document behavior clearly.
next_steps:
1) Address PR feedback: add OneOf example and metadata param to EnvelopeUnwrap.
2) Add remaining integration tests and a small example app in examples/structured-chat.
3) Request SDK API review and runtime compatibility sign-off.
4) Merge behind feature flag for one release, monitor telemetry (errors and retries) from canary customers.
notes_for_release:
- Add migration notes to CHANGELOG describing new ErrTruncatedStream and default retransmitOnTruncated behavior.
- Document new contracts package and include small quickstart snippet in README.
- Toggle in runtime to opt-out of retransmit for legacy Dedicated deployments if needed.
